_comment: SHARED MODULE REGISTRY — the single list of every game, GoodBlock and Challenge.
Plain JSON so a browser page can fetch() it and a Node script can read it with fs.
Consumers today: public/dashboard/index.html (MODULE_REGISTRY), the three Lab Pack hubs
(public/jsh/*/index.html), public/js/skill-routing.js (the shared game -> GoodBlock
resolver) and scripts/check-modules.js (which validates every other surface against it).
FIELDS
id          module slug; matches Telemetry.init({ module }) and Insider's COURSES id.
name        display name; must match the dashboard card and Insider exactly.
type        'game' | 'lab' | 'challenge'.
pack        pack id for labs/challenges. ALWAYS null for a game: a game routes across
packs depending on which skill a student is weak in, so it belongs to none.
url         site-relative, trailing-slash. null for a retired module with no live page.
skillTags   [{ framework, code }]. framework 'internal' is the ROUTING vocabulary —
the category system Read the Signal proved out. 'CASEL' / 'ISTE' ride along
for reporting and are ported verbatim from the coverage-map docs in
docs/goodblocks/ — nothing here was invented. A tag may carry its own
"status": "draft" when that ONE tag is new this sprint and unreviewed,
even on an entry whose other tags are signed off.
An `alias_of` on a tag means the scenario bank spells that category two
ways (Read the Signal has both `safe` and `safe-recognition` in its bank)
and both must resolve; it is not a second skill. Registered rather than
renamed, because relabelling a live game's working categories is not
this sprint's job.
evidence    REQUIRED on every internal tag: where this placement comes from. Either the
shipped routing that already proved it, or the coverage-map Case it rests on.
scripts/check-modules.js fails the build on an internal tag without one.
This exists because of a real bug: `reputation` was placed on Social
Intelligence by content-similarity judgment, with nothing recording why and
nothing able to check it, and The Rumor Mill routed there on staging. Social
Intelligence does not teach reputational harm — Digital Citizenship does. A
placement nobody can cite is a placement nobody can review.
hidden      OPTIONAL, boolean. TRUE means the module is live and registered but must
NOT be surfaced on any of this site's own surfaces: no main-nav link, no
games-hub card, no dashboard card, no Lab Pack hub entry, and not
assignable in Mission Control. It is registered ANYWAY, deliberately, for
two reasons: leaving it out of the registry means check-modules.js can
verify nothing about it, and a future session finding an unregistered live
module will read it as a bug and "fix" it by surfacing it. A hidden module
is exempted from the must-appear-on-a-surface checks and from NOTHING
else — id uniqueness, url resolving, required fields and Telemetry.init are
all still enforced, and check-modules.js additionally asserts that it is
ABSENT from every surface. Same shape as `orphanedSkills`: an explicit,
visible exemption the build knows about, never a silent skip.
hiddenSince REQUIRED when hidden is true. YYYY-MM-DD, the date it was hidden.
hiddenReason REQUIRED when hidden is true. Why this module is off the site's own
surfaces, so the decision can be reviewed instead of guessed at.
status      'reviewed' when the entry's skill tagging has a sign-off behind it,
'draft' when this sprint proposed it and Curriculum & Learning Science has
not yet reviewed it.
ORPHANED SKILLS (top-level `orphanedSkills`, a sibling of `modules`)
A game diagnosing a skill that no GoodBlock teaches is normally a BUILD FAILURE: the
routing silently stops adapting and nobody finds out. That default stays. This list is
the one narrow exception — a skill we KNOW has no teaching destination, said out loud
here rather than hidden by inventing a fake destination to quiet the check.
Being on this list downgrades the failure to a warning that check-modules.js prints on
every run. It is a debt register, not an ignore file: an entry must carry `tag`,
`since` and a `reason` saying what the pending decision is. Remove the entry the
moment a GoodBlock teaches the skill — check-modules.js fails on a stale one, so this
list cannot quietly outlive the gap it documents.
Presentation fields (gameNames, topic, blurb, durationMinutes, badgeThreshold, maxScore,
hub) are a straight port of what the dashboard and hubs already rendered. Tailwind class
names deliberately stay in the HTML templates that use them: the CSS build's content globs
scan public/**/*.html and public/js/**/*.js, NOT .json, so a class moved here would be
purged out of the bundle. Only data (icon name, hex colors, copy) lives here.
isComplete() predicates stay in the dashboard — a JSON file cannot hold a function.

orphanedSkills.reason: Removed from Social Intelligence — the placement was a content-similarity guess (Case 5's "warm private check-in" read as emotional disclosure). Case 5's actual mechanic is audience choice: public counter-attack vs. private support. No GoodBlock currently teaches vulnerability, and Before You Send has 8 scenarios diagnosing it. Pending a Curriculum & Learning Science decision on whether to build content for it or fold it into an existing GoodBlock; not resolvable by re-tagging.

modules.name: Pattern Lab
modules.hiddenReason: Free CogAT-style practice diagnostic for grades 5-8, published for parents arriving from search. Its absence from this site's own surfaces is the design, not an oversight: the audience is a parent who just got a testing letter from their school, not a teacher browsing allgoodacademy.com, and surfacing it in the nav or on the games hub would put a product with no classroom use in front of the one audience it is not written for. Its only inbound links are /pattern-lab/ and search. It also has no internal skillTags on purpose — its nine subtests are not in the routing vocabulary and must never resolve to a GoodBlock (see the guard in public/js/skill-routing.js).
